en.title: Fill in Colors to Maximize Single-Color Substrings
en.description:
Replace every dot with a letter from a..z to maximize the number of contiguous substrings whose characters are all the same. Substrings of length 1 also count, and fixed characters cannot be changed.

The input/output protocol and the explicitly marked supplementary constraints were compiled by this site; upstream solutions are not executed.
en.input: One line containing the color string, of length 1..5000, where each character is a..z or a dot (.). Output the exact integer.
en.output: Output the single integer required by the problem.
en.explanation: The answers to the three public examples are, in order: 4; 6; 11. The examples were rechecked by independent enumeration, state search, or direct simulation.
hints: Decompose the filled string into single-color runs; a run of length l contributes l(l+1)/2. Use a prefix DP that enumerates the last run, scanning backward and stopping as soon as a second distinct fixed letter is met.
